title: Regular completed coefficients and the quotient Koszul fiber
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $O$ and uniformizer $\pi$, and a scheme $T$. On $T_{\mathrm{proét}}$ put $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$ for $n\geq1$, with their projections and quotient transitions [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Use cochain derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. There are a unit $u\in O^\times$ and $e\geq1$ with $\ell=u\pi^e$; the two sequences of ideals are cofinal. The rings $O/\pi^j$ and $O/\ell^n$ are finite for all $j,n\geq1$. The canonical maps identify $R/\ell^nR=B_n$ and $R/\pi^jR=(O/\pi^j)_T$. Multiplication by every $\ell^m$ and $\pi^j$ is injective on $R$. The augmented two-term complexes $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^m}R]\to B_m$ and $L_j=[R\xrightarrow{\pi^j}R]\to(O/\pi^j)_T$, in degrees $[-1,0]$, are finite free K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex].

For $n\geq m\geq1$ set $P_{n,m}=B_n\otimes_RK_m=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell^m}B_n]$, with augmentation $\epsilon_{n,m}:P_{n,m}\to B_m$ given by reduction in degree zero, and $F_{n,m}=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_{n,m})[-1]$. The map $B_m[1]\to F_{n,m}$ with degree $-1$ coordinate $x\mapsto\ell^{n-m}x$ in $P_{n,m}^{-1}$ (and zero other coordinates) is a quasi-isomorphism of $B_n$-complexes. In particular $H^{-1}(P_{n,m})=\ell^{n-m}B_n\cong B_m$ and $H^0(P_{n,m})=B_m$. For $n'\geq n\geq m$, the coefficient reduction $F_{n',m}\to F_{n,m}$ corresponds under these quasi-isomorphisms to multiplication by $\ell^{n'-n}$ on $B_m[1]$. These statements include $n=m$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $O$ is a DVR with finite residue field and every nonzero element of $E$ is a unit times an integer power of $\pi$. Apply this to $\ell$. Since $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$ and $0<|\pi|_E<1$, its exponent $e$ is positive: $\ell=u\pi^e$ with $u\in O^\times$, $e\geq1$. Thus $(\ell^n)=(\pi^{en})$, which proves cofinality (for each $j$, choose $n$ with $en\geq j$; for each $n$, choose $j=en$). The hypotheses of [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] hold: $|\cdot|_E$ is nonarchimedean by clause 1 of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $O$ is a DVR with maximal ideal $\{|x|_E<1\}$, finite residue field and uniformizer $\pi$ by the clauses just cited. Its finite-quotient clause gives finiteness of $O/\pi^j$, and $O/\ell^n=O/\pi^{en}$ is finite as well.

proof.text: Clause (3) of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], for the given arbitrary scheme $T$ and finite extension $E$, identifies the pulled-back ring $R$ with the inverse limit of the uniformizer-power constant quotient sheaves, with their reduction projections. These are precisely the coefficient projections of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Apply [lem-pod-completed-integral-scalar-regular] to this inverse-limit sheaf: for every site object $U$, multiplication by $\pi^j$ on $R(U)$ is injective. The image of the constant unit $u$ in $R(U)$ is invertible, so $\ell^m=u^m\pi^{em}$ also acts injectively. This is sectionwise injectivity, hence injectivity as a sheaf map; no hypothesis on the characteristic, dimension or finiteness of $T$ has been used.

source.place: Coefficient tensor-product calculation in the first paragraph, expanded at chain level

proof.text: Write $\rho_j:R\to(O/\pi^j)_T$ for a projection. It kills $\pi^jR$, and [lem-sp-completed-integral-projection-divisibility], with its index $j-1\geq0$, says conversely that every section in its kernel is $\pi^j$ times a section of $R$. The projection is locally surjective: by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], a target section locally comes from a single element of $O/\pi^j$; choose an $O$-representative $a$, and its compatible residue classes define a section of the inverse limit mapping to that element. Consequently the induced map $R/\pi^jR\to(O/\pi^j)_T$ is locally bijective, hence an isomorphism of sheaves: local inverses agree on overlaps by injectivity and glue uniquely. Because all maps come from the same compatible residue projections, they preserve ring operations and quotient transitions. Substituting $j=en$ and using $\ell^nR=\pi^{en}R$ gives the canonical identification $R/\ell^nR=B_n$. This proves the genuine sheaf quotient assertion, not merely the notation stipulated in [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers].

source.place: Coefficient tensor-product calculation in the first paragraph, expanded at chain level

proof.text: The two-term complexes have $H^{-1}=0$ by scalar injectivity, and $H^0$ equal to their indicated quotients by step 3. Thus their augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms, by the cohomology definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Each is the mapping cone of the corresponding scalar map $R[0]\to R[0]$. For any acyclic complex $A$, the total tensor $A\otimes_RR[0]$ is $A$ by the unit identification, directly from [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Both copies are therefore acyclic. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-tensor-cone-two-out-of-three] on the ringed site $(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ to conclude that its tensor with the cone is acyclic. This is exactly K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Their two nonzero terms are $R$, so these are finite free K-flat resolutions.

source.place: Tag 07A3, lemma-K-flat-two-out-of-three; Definition 06YN; applied to the scalar cone

proof.text: Tensoring $K_m$ with $B_n[0]$ using [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives exactly $P_{n,m}=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell^m}B_n]$. Reduction $B_n\to B_m$ kills its differential since $n\geq m$, so $\epsilon_{n,m}$ is a chain map. Define $a_{n,m}:B_m\to B_n$ by $\bar x\mapsto\ell^{n-m}\bar x$: locally lift $\bar x$ to $R$; changing the lift by $\ell^my$ changes the answer by $\ell^ny=0$ in $B_n$. These local formulas agree and glue. They are $B_n$-linear, with $B_m$ carrying its reduction action.

source.place: Coefficient tensor-product calculation in the first paragraph, expanded at chain level

proof.text: The map $a_{n,m}$ identifies $B_m$ with $\ker(\ell^m:B_n\to B_n)$. Indeed, locally lift a section $\bar x\in B_n$ to $x\in R$. If $\ell^m\bar x=0$, then, after a further cover if needed, $\ell^m x=\ell^ny$ for some $y\in R$. Cancellation of the injective scalar $\ell^m$ gives $x=\ell^{n-m}y$, proving local surjectivity onto the kernel. If $\ell^{n-m}y=\ell^nz$, cancellation gives $y=\ell^mz$, proving injectivity (when $n=m$ this cancels the identity). Also $\operatorname{im}(\ell^m:B_n\to B_n)=\ker(B_n\to B_m)$: both are locally the residue classes represented by $\ell^my$, and reduction is locally surjective. Hence $H^{-1}(P_{n,m})=\ell^{n-m}B_n\cong B_m$ and $H^0(P_{n,m})=B_m$, by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Coefficient tensor-product calculation in the first paragraph, expanded at chain level

proof.text: Use the cone and shift signs of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In degrees $-1,0,1$, the shifted cone $F_{n,m}=\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon_{n,m})[-1]$ is the three-term complex $B_n\xrightarrow{\ell^m}B_n\xrightarrow{-\mathrm{red}}B_m$, zero elsewhere. The map $i_{n,m}:B_m[1]\to F_{n,m}$ has degree $-1$ component $a_{n,m}$ and all other components zero; it is a chain map since $\ell^m\ell^{n-m}=\ell^n=0$ in $B_n$. Step 6 says that $H^{-1}(i_{n,m})$ is an isomorphism. It also gives $H^0(F_{n,m})=\ker(\mathrm{red})/\operatorname{im}(\ell^m)=0$ and $H^1(F_{n,m})=\operatorname{coker}(-\mathrm{red})=0$. All remaining cohomology vanishes by the displayed terms. Thus $i_{n,m}$ is the specified quasi-isomorphism of $B_n$-complexes.

source.place: Coefficient tensor-product calculation in the first paragraph, expanded at chain level

proof.text: For $n'\geq n\geq m$, coefficient reduction on both terms of $P$ commutes with $\epsilon$ and induces on the three displayed terms of $F$ the maps $(\mathrm{red},\mathrm{red},1_{B_m})$. The formula for the cone in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives this chain map directly, with no choice of cone morphism. For any local lift $x\in R$ of a section of $B_m$, its degree $-1$ component sends $\ell^{n'-m}x\bmod\ell^{n'}$ to $\ell^{n'-m}x\bmod\ell^n$, which equals $\ell^{n-m}(\ell^{n'-n}x)\bmod\ell^n$. All other components of $i$ are zero. Therefore the chain-level square is exactly $F_{n',m}\to F_{n,m}$ composed with $i_{n',m}$ equals $i_{n,m}$ composed with $\ell^{n'-n}:B_m[1]\to B_m[1]$ (viewing both sources by restriction to $B_{n'}$). Inverting the quasi-isomorphisms proves the claimed transition formula. For $n=m$, $\ell^m=0$ in $B_m$, $a_{m,m}=1$, and the remaining two-term summand is $B_m\xrightarrow{-1}B_m$, so the same computation includes the boundary case.
